quickAnswer: Non-resident visitors can claim Turkish VAT (KDV) refunds on unused goods costing at least 1,000 TRY before tax per receipt, exported within three months. At Istanbul Airport (IST), validate checked-baggage items before security at counters G3–G5 or K25–K27, and hand-luggage purchases at the customs desk after passport control.
category: Practical Travel Logistics, Money, Visas & Transport

body.text: Purchases in Istanbul—from Nişantaşı leather ateliers to Zorlu Center boutiques—include 10% or 20% Turkish VAT (KDV). Recovering that tax at Istanbul Airport (IST) works smoothly when you collect proper store paperwork and inspect goods at the right customs counter before flying out.
What is the minimum spend for VAT refunds in Türkiye?

The minimum qualifying purchase for tax free shopping in Türkiye is 1,000 TRY plus VAT on a single invoice from a participating retailer. You must live permanently outside Türkiye, stay fewer than six consecutive months, and carry the unused goods out of the country in your personal luggage within three months of the invoice date.
Türkiye applies two main VAT tiers on tourist purchases, as confirmed by [Global Blue Türkiye](https://www.globalblue.com/en/shoppers/how-to-shop-tax-free/destinations/turkey):
Intermediaries deduct handling commissions, and airport cash desks apply conversion spreads. Request a credit card refund in Turkish lira to keep more of your tax back.
Which shops issue Global Blue or Planet Tax Free forms?

Major international boutiques, Istanbul shopping malls (İstinyePark, Zorlu Center, Kanyon), upscale Nişantaşı showrooms, and established carpet or jewellery houses issue [Global Blue](https://www.globalblue.com/en/shoppers/how-to-shop-tax-free/destinations/turkey) or [Planet Tax Free](https://taxfree.weareplanet.com/countries/turkey) forms. Smaller neighbourhood workshops and Grand Bazaar stalls rarely participate unless they hold a special export-invoice licence, so confirm eligibility before you pay.
Carry your passport when shopping and check four details at checkout:

items: Exact passport match: Full name, passport number, and home address must match your passport with zero typos.
Itemised invoice attached: Ensure the original Turkish fatura is stapled to the tax-free form.
Digital barcode: Use the [Global Blue Shop Tax Free app](https://www.globalblue.com/en/shoppers/global-blue-shop-tax-free-app) to pre-fill details and track card payouts.
Single-invoice threshold: The 1,000 TRY pre-tax minimum applies per receipt, not combined across shops.

body.text: Where are the customs stamp desks at IST before and after security?

Istanbul Airport splits customs validation strictly by how you pack your purchases. According to [iGA Istanbul Airport's official Tax Refunds guide](https://www.istairport.com/en/services/discover/airport-facilities/tax-refunds?locale=en), checked-luggage items are inspected before security at Check-in Counters G3–G5 (Turkish Airlines) or K25–K27 (other airlines), whereas carry-on purchases are stamped after passport control in the right-hand corner.
Follow the right lane for your bags:

items: Checked luggage: Collect your boarding pass and bag tags at check-in, take the tagged suitcase to counters G3–G5 (Turkish Airlines) or K25–K27 (other carriers) for inspection, then drop it there once stamped.
Hand luggage: Clear security and passport control, then visit the customs desk in the right-hand corner.

Payouts: Present stamped forms at the [Global Exchange counters](https://www.istairport.com/en/services/discover/airport-facilities/tax-refunds?locale=en) behind the airside information desk or at Global Blue and Planet kiosks. Keep watches and jewellery in carry-on.

body.text: How long before your flight should you arrive to claim a refund?

Arrive at Istanbul Airport at least 3.5 to 4 hours before international departure if you are claiming VAT refunds on checked luggage, and 3 hours ahead for hand-luggage claims alone. Peak morning (06:00–09:30) and late-evening (21:00–01:00) long-haul banks create 30-to-60-minute bottlenecks at both customs validation and refund payout windows.

Walking from airside refund counters to distant F or A gates takes 18–25 minutes. For bulky carpets or multi-stop trips, see our guide to [luggage storage and shipping across Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/luggage-storage-istanbul).

faq.q: Can I claim a VAT refund on items I have already worn or used in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Turkish customs rules require all tax-free purchases to be completely unused, with original tags and packaging intact, ready for physical inspection at the airport.

faq.q: Can I get my VAT refund in euros or US dollars at Istanbul Airport?
faq.a: Yes, airside refund counters pay cash in TRY, EUR, or USD, though exchange rates and cash-handling fees reduce your net return. Selecting a credit card refund in TRY usually yields a better final amount.

faq.q: How long does a Global Blue or Planet credit card refund take?
faq.a: Card refunds typically post within 5 to 15 business days after customs validation, though busy summer periods can stretch processing to 3 to 4 weeks. Keep photos of every stamped form until the credit lands.

faq.q: What if I am flying out of Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW) instead of IST?
faq.a: Sabiha Gökçen also has customs validation and refund desks in its international departures terminal. Arrive at least 3 hours early, as SAW operates fewer customs counters than IST.

faq.q: Do Turkish carpets shipped home by courier qualify for airport VAT refunds?
faq.a: No. Airport VAT refunds apply only to goods carried in your personal luggage. Reputable carpet dealers who export directly via DHL or FedEx issue a VAT-exempt export invoice at the point of sale instead.

faq.q: What happens if I forget to get a customs stamp before leaving Türkiye?
faq.a: Without a Turkish customs validation stamp (or digital customs confirmation) recorded upon departure, neither Global Blue nor Planet can issue a refund. Stamps cannot be obtained retroactively after you leave the country.
